title: A loaded save reuses freed slotmap slots in a different order than the uninterrupted game
description: Playtest staging (2026-10-16): a save at day 60 loaded and run 15 days diverges from the straight run (fingerprints cd7111ed2f3840a8 vs 654f1a00678d424a; equal at +10). A world JSON diff shows exactly one difference: a new manufacturing facility at manufacturing_facilities[47] version 3 (freed slot reused) in the straight run, [99] version 2 (fresh slot) after load. Every other world field matches, and the restored sim_rng and the other states are identical. So the slotmap free list is not restored in its pre-save order, and since the AI walks the world's slotmap order (e.g. ai_production scrap_system_fighter after the 2026-10-16 determinism fix) a loaded game plays differently. Fix: persist and restore each slotmap's free order (save bump), or allocate new objects in an order independent of slot reuse. Gate: agent_docs/simulation.md --load paragraph; hyp: the replay golden's save-reload test passes because its window frees no slot before the save (unverified).
notes: Fixed: world slotmaps are saved as {slots, free} (crates/rebellion-core/src/world/slot_order.rs, serde(with) on the 11 GameWorld arenas, save v48). slotmap's serde keeps slots+versions but rebuilds the free list in descending index order; the adapter writes the pop order (probed on a clone) and rebuilds each map by remove/insert cycles to saved versions, freeing vacant slots in reverse pop order; rejects a free list that is not a permutation of the vacant slots. Proof (same binary): seed 42 and 7 save@60 +15 == straight 75; seed 42 save@300 +700 == straight 1000; seed 7 save@300 +300 == straight 600. Seed 7 straight runs are themselves nondeterministic between day 600 and 700 (same binary, three different fingerprints), unrelated to load. Replay golden: initial fingerprint no longer matches (free order is now in the canonical fingerprint); not regenerated.

title: Match Direct3D RM's 8-bit palette, line stepping and rasterizer for the tactical aperture
description:
Match Direct3D Retained Mode's 8-bit output so the tactical aperture's SSIM and edge IoU can pass, starting with TAC-05-C019.

The original draws the tactical scene through d3drm.dll, a system library outside the executable's trace, into an 8-bit paletted surface. A0 TAC-05-C019 (empire-death-star-pre-alert, day 676) holds 69 colours in the whole frame and 21 to 24 in the aperture (TAC-05-C017 21, TAC-05-C019 24).

What the port must match:
- Colour matching: every 3D pixel maps into the display palette. The scene background's greys (resource 5030, palette 5553) read 24, 40 and 58 in the port; A0 shows 0, 48 and 48.
- The scene background stretch: SetSceneBackgroundImage (frame slot 0xcc) draws the 440 by 438 image into the 439 by 437 viewport at (17, 30). Stars land one to two pixels from an unscaled copy, some as 2 by 2 blocks.
- The wireframe line stepping for the holocube (quality 0x40).
- Flat-shaded mesh rasterization and the scene's lights for the capital meshes.

Measured on C019 with the traced camera, 3D window and holocube (or-p-tactical-camera-viewport-aw39): 7,466 aperture edge pixels in A0 or A1, of which 5,350 coincide (edge IoU 0.717). The misses split as holocube 361, ships, fighters and strike 1,016, stars 739. Passing edge IoU 0.98 allows about 150.

C019 passes the C6 position measures (displacement, MAE, changed pixels) under a split recorded in tactical-a0-compare.json; its SSIM and edge IoU rows wait on this node.

title: Port: per-side views for the AI system record (FUN_0050fc80, FUN_0050d5a0)
description:
The AI system record (`ai_records::fill_system`, `FUN_00433e40.c:120-125`) stops at Q `0x80` when the side's view of the system lacks `+0x88` bit 1. `FUN_0050fc80` copies that bit, with bit 0 (populated, `FUN_0050fbf0`), into a side's view while the view is live, and an observation level refresh (`FUN_0050d5a0`: informants, espionage, mission ends) copies it too; a view that stops being live keeps the bit (`ghidra/notes/observation-levels.md`).

The port has no per-side views. `fill_system` reads the bit as held for a core system (SYSTEMSD family `0x90`), a system the side holds, and one where it has a usable fleet (`hyp:` in its doc). It misses a view kept from an earlier observation and every observation-level refresh. The world's `exploration_status` cannot stand in: either side's intelligence mission sets it (integrator `SystemIntelligenceGathered`), which leaked the other side's espionage into this side's record.

Port: keep per side which systems' views hold bit 1 (set when the view goes live and on each `FUN_0050d5a0` refresh, never cleared) and have `fill_system` read the side's own. Save-format change (SAVE_VERSION bump). Both factions.

title: Q: How does a system change sides in the original, and what does FUN_0050b610 compute?
description: economy.rs resolve_system_control reads FUN_0050b610 as the control rule (troops of one side only -> that side controls; none and low energy -> uncontrolled). The decompile (ghidra/notes/FUN_0050b610.c) builds a 2-bit field (local_30 >> 4 & 3) from the two sides' regiment queries (FUN_00504cc0 side 1 and 2, FUN_005131b0) and nothing in it writes control. In the port no diplomacy success ever makes a neutral system join a side: a 400-day dual-AI playtest (seed 42) ends with Alliance 2 systems, Empire 3, neutral 95, as a run from before the AI port did; 195 Diplomacy missions, several successes, one control change (Drall to Uncontrolled); on day 1 Corellia, Vagran and Xyquine drop to Uncontrolled. The stalled economy starves the AI: the Alliance's maintenance capacity stays 100 (load 87), module 6's facility budget is 4 against a training facility's 10, so it never builds one and never trains a regiment, and module 8's postures never get the regiment surplus their assault and drop targets need. Settle in the original (VM): what makes a neutral system join a side (support threshold? GNPRTB?), and what the FUN_0050b610 field feeds. Game-rule code: explain before changing. Done when the port follows the original for both sides, verified e2e.
notes:
2026-10-15: now also blocks or-glv7: with the original AI ported, the starved economy leaves both sides without a fleet to attack (no Move of a fleet, no battle in 1000 days). Settling this rule is the next step for the AI's e2e.
2026-10-15 decompile reading: FUN_0050b610 rebuilds the system control word (+0x84, validated by FUN_00558880). Bits 2-3, the support side: 3 when +0x88 bit 0 (populated) is clear, else FUN_0055a080(sys+0x58) = 1 when Alliance support >= DAT_006bb4c0, 2 when 100 - support >= it, else 3 (neutral). DAT_006bb4c0 is GNPRTB 0x1e50 = 7760 (60), loaded in FUN_00558bb0. Bits 4-5, the troop side (FUN_00504cc0 regiment queries per side, FUN_005131b0): 1 Alliance only, 2 Empire only, unchanged when both, 0 when none. The holder (bits 0-1, FUN_005588f0) is the troop side when bits 4-5 are set, else the support side; FUN_0050a300 commits it. So a system without troops belongs to the side whose support reaches 60, neutral between 41 and 59. The port's resolve_system_control compares total_energy with GNPRTB 7760 instead, and with no troops keeps or clears control; that is why no system ever joins a side.
